name: Bombardier Challenger 600 series
summary: Wide-cabin large business jet in production since 1980; the CRJ regional airliner is a stretched development of the same design.

wings: Low swept wing with upturned winglets (601 onward)
engines: Two GE CF34 turbofans (Lycoming ALF502 on the original 600) in pods on the rear fuselage
fuselage: Short, very wide and deep fuselage that looks fat for its length
Prominent belly fairing under the wing center section

tellTales: Short, fat wide-body fuselage on a T-tail twinjet
Prominent belly fairing under the wing root
Upturned winglets and engines high on the rear fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: The Challenger 600 is much shorter with fewer, larger windows; the CRJ200 is a long stretch with many small airliner windows and overwing exits.
The Challenger 600-series is fatter and deeper with a belly fairing; the Challenger 300/350 is slimmer with a long tapered tail cone.
The Challenger 600 has a T-tail; the Falcon 2000 has its tailplane partway up the fin.
The Challenger 600 is short and fat with rounded-rectangle windows; the GIV/G550 is long and slim with oval windows.

usCount.source: Bombardier production (~1,150 CL-600 to 650) with ~45% active US-registered per JETNET fleet summaries (approx.)
